title: How to Learn Responsibly About Palestine
subtitle: A practical method for sources, images, dates, and uncertainty — Written for sincere seekers asking whether Islam is true.
summary: For sincere seekers asking whether Islam is true: Information about Palestine can be emotionally powerful and rapidly shared. This draft gives a simple method for checking authorship, dates, evidence, imagery, and uncertainty before accepting or passing on a claim.

sections.title: For a Seeker Asking Whether Islam Is True
sections.body:
This article is written for a sincere seeker asking whether Islam is true. It is not only a neutral comparison or an interfaith description.

Reliable investigation of Islam requires primary texts, transparent source labels, and honest acknowledgment of uncertainty; careful method serves the truth-seeking question rather than replacing it.

Where historians or scholars disagree, the article identifies the main alternatives before drawing its Islamic implication.

Read the labels carefully: an explicit Quranic or Prophetic text, an established Sunni teaching, a classical or modern scholarly interpretation, a historical reconstruction, and the author's inference are different kinds of claim. Disputed questions should be identified as disputed rather than hidden.

sections.title: In Plain Words
sections.body:
Slow down before sharing. Ask who made the claim, when it was made, what evidence it gives, and whether an independent source confirms it. A true concern for people does not require repeating an unverified claim.

The same standards should be used for sources that agree with you and sources that do not. That is how a reader protects both truth and human dignity.

sections.title: Five Questions to Ask
sections.body:
First, who is the original source: a witness, an official body, a researcher, or an account repeating someone else? Second, what is the date and location? Third, what evidence is provided, and can it be checked? Fourth, does the wording distinguish fact, allegation, and opinion? Fifth, has a credible independent source confirmed the central claim?

Images and video require extra care. A real image may be old, from another location, cropped, or paired with a false caption. If the original cannot be located, describe it as unverified rather than treating it as proof.

sections.title: Read Across Difference
sections.body:
Read primary documents where possible, then compare historians, legal scholars, human-rights organisations, and reporting organisations with transparent methods. Notice what a source is qualified to establish and what it is not. A devotional text can explain a community's religious attachment; it cannot by itself settle a disputed historical claim.

Responsible learning does not mean pretending every claim has equal evidence. It means stating the evidence, the source's perspective, and any uncertainty plainly.

sections.title: A Worked Example
sections.body:
Suppose a post shares a photograph and says it was taken in a particular city during a particular week. First locate the earliest upload, inspect image-search or metadata evidence where available, and compare the visible landmarks with older photographs. Then check whether a reputable news organisation, eyewitness account, or official record confirms the date and place. Until that chain is established, the careful description is 'the image's date and location are unverified'—not 'the image proves the claim.'

The same method applies to casualty figures or quotations. Record who first made the assertion, distinguish a reported number from a confirmed number, and check whether independent sources are actually independent rather than repeating one another.

sections.title: What This Means for a Seeker
sections.body:
This article is one part of a larger truth-seeking case. Its subject should not be treated as an isolated proof or as a reason to stop at comparison. The Islamic claim is that the Quran restores clear guidance about the one God and calls human beings to respond to Him with faith, worship, repentance, and moral responsibility.

Reliable investigation of Islam requires primary texts, transparent source labels, and honest acknowledgment of uncertainty; careful method serves the truth-seeking question rather than replacing it.

If you are asking whether Islam is true, take a direct next step: read the Quran itself in a reliable translation, revisit the primary sources linked here, and write down the strongest objection that remains. Ask God sincerely for guidance and take that question to a trustworthy, knowledgeable Muslim. The aim is not to win an interfaith argument or to caricature alternatives, but to investigate Islam honestly and then respond to its claim.

faq.question: If I am asking whether Islam is true, what should I do next?
faq.answer: Begin with the Quran in a reliable translation and the primary sources linked in this article. Ask God sincerely for guidance, note the strongest question that remains, and discuss it with a trustworthy, knowledgeable Muslim. Reliable investigation of Islam requires primary texts, transparent source labels, and honest acknowledgment of uncertainty; careful method serves the truth-seeking question rather than replacing it.
